description: The size of each funding source is measured by how many spatial records it has.

b.request: Group spatial records by funding source, treating NULL as its own group; for each group, calculate the average non-NULL `boxy / boxz` ratio and record count. Keep groups whose count exceeds the average count across funding source groups, then return one row with the average of those groups’ ratio averages, their combined record count, and the average amount by which their counts exceed the average group count, without rounding
b.sql:
WITH funding_group_stats AS (
  SELECT
    p.fundflux,
    AVG(ss.boxy / NULLIF(ss.boxz, 0)) AS avg_ratio,
    COUNT(*) AS record_count
  FROM scanspatial AS ss
  JOIN projects AS p ON p.arcregistry = ss.arcref
  GROUP BY p.fundflux
),
average_group_count AS (
  SELECT AVG(record_count) AS avg_count
  FROM funding_group_stats
),
above_average_groups AS (
  SELECT fgs.avg_ratio, fgs.record_count, agc.avg_count
  FROM funding_group_stats AS fgs
  CROSS JOIN average_group_count AS agc
  WHERE fgs.record_count > agc.avg_count
)
SELECT
  AVG(avg_ratio) AS average_of_group_ratio_averages,
  SUM(record_count) AS combined_record_count,
  AVG(record_count - avg_count) AS average_excess_count
FROM above_average_groups;

a.request: Using spatial records (`scanspatial`) matched to a project (`projects.arcregistry` = `scanspatial.arcref`), for each funding source (`projects.fundflux`, treating a missing source as its own group) compute the average ratio of bounding box Y (`boxy`) to bounding box Z (`boxz`), ignoring missing values, and the number of spatial records. Keep the funding sources whose number of spatial records is above the average of that number across all funding sources. Return one row with: the average of the kept sources' ratios; the total of their spatial record counts; and the average amount by which their counts exceed the cross-source average. No rounding.
a.sql:
WITH source_stats AS (
  SELECT
    p.fundflux,
    AVG(ss.boxy / NULLIF(ss.boxz, 0)) AS avg_ratio,
    COUNT(*) AS record_count
  FROM projects AS p
  JOIN scanspatial AS ss ON ss.arcref = p.arcregistry
  GROUP BY p.fundflux
),
threshold AS (
  SELECT AVG(record_count) AS avg_count
  FROM source_stats
),
kept AS (
  SELECT s.avg_ratio, s.record_count, t.avg_count
  FROM source_stats AS s
  CROSS JOIN threshold AS t
  WHERE s.record_count > t.avg_count
)
SELECT
  AVG(avg_ratio) AS average_ratio,
  SUM(record_count) AS total_spatial_records,
  AVG(record_count - avg_count) AS average_excess_count
FROM kept;

c.request: Looking at spatial scan data (`scanspatial`) linked to projects (`projects.arcregistry` = `scanspatial.arcref`), which funding sources (`projects.fundflux`, treating a missing source as its own group) are bigger than average? For each funding source, work out the average ratio of bounding box Y (`boxy`) to bounding box Z (`boxz`), ignoring missing values, and how big it is. For the sources above the average size across funding sources, give one row with the average of their ratios, their combined size, and how far on average they exceed the average size. No rounding. The size of each funding source is measured by how many spatial records it has.
c.sql:
WITH funding_stats AS (
  SELECT p.fundflux,
         AVG(ss.boxy / NULLIF(ss.boxz, 0)) AS avg_ratio,
         COUNT(*) AS source_size
  FROM projects AS p
  JOIN scanspatial AS ss ON ss.arcref = p.arcregistry
  GROUP BY p.fundflux
),
with_average AS (
  SELECT funding_stats.*,
         AVG(source_size) OVER () AS average_size
  FROM funding_stats
)
SELECT AVG(avg_ratio) AS avg_ratio,
       SUM(source_size) AS combined_size,
       AVG(source_size - average_size) AS avg_excess_size
FROM with_average
WHERE source_size > average_size;

d.request: For each funding source, including missing funding sources as their own group, count its linked spatial records and calculate the average `boxy`/`boxz` ratio, ignoring missing values. Which funding sources have a record count above the average count across all funding sources? For those sources, return one row with the average of their ratios, their combined record count, and their average excess over the average funding source record count. Do not round the results.
d.sql:
WITH source_stats AS (
  SELECT
    p.fundflux,
    COUNT(ss.domainregistry) AS record_count,
    AVG(ss.boxy / NULLIF(ss.boxz, 0)) AS avg_ratio
  FROM projects AS p
  LEFT JOIN scanspatial AS ss
    ON ss.arcref = p.arcregistry
  GROUP BY p.fundflux
),
qualified_sources AS (
  SELECT *
  FROM source_stats
  WHERE record_count > (SELECT AVG(record_count) FROM source_stats)
)
SELECT
  AVG(avg_ratio) AS average_ratio,
  SUM(record_count) AS combined_record_count,
  AVG(record_count - (SELECT AVG(record_count) FROM source_stats)) AS average_excess_record_count
FROM qualified_sources;
